Driftwood CLI · v3.2 docs

Build static sites from Markdown

Quick start

Create a site, write a page and preview it locally in under five minutes.

  1. Create a project. The starter includes a home page, a blog folder and a default theme. 
    npx driftwood new field-notes
  2. Write your first page. Any .md file inside content/ becomes a page with the same path.
  3. Start the preview server. Pages reload as you save. 
    cd field-notes && npx driftwood dev

Tip: run driftwood build when you are ready. The finished site lands in dist/.

Installation

Driftwood runs anywhere Node.js 20 or newer is available. Add it to an existing project as a dev dependency:

npm install --save-dev driftwood

Requirements

  • Node.js 20.10 or later
  • About 40 MB of disk space for the default theme
  • macOS, Linux or Windows 10 and later

Upgrading from v2? Front matter keys are now lowercase. Run driftwood migrate once to rename them.

Configuration

Settings live in driftwood.config.js at the project root. Every key is optional.

Option Type Default
title string Folder name
baseUrl string /
outDir string dist
drafts boolean false

API reference

Use the build API to run Driftwood from your own scripts.

build(options?: BuildOptions): Promise<BuildResult>
options.root
Project folder. Defaults to the current working directory.
options.watch
Rebuild on change and resolve only when stopped.
BuildResult.pages
Number of pages written, handy for CI logs.
